S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every known thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with an initial account even if facts remain incomplete. Affected customers must be notified within 72 hours when the incident presents a credible safety risk to their unit or requires customer action.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Manufacturers must provide complete per-model results, including failure rates, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model. A failure rate above 5% requires a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retesting within 12 months; it does not by itself require market exclusion.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery units placed on the market must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that lack this capability, or provide an equally effective regulator-approved mitigation, within six years after adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and submit an investigation and corrective-action proposal. The regulator must assess the evidence and may require a mandatory recall or other safeguards where warranted, including earlier action where evidence indicates an imminent risk.

document.section_notes: S2 keeps per-model failure rates confidential to the regulator and disclosed only to purchasers of that model, and a rate above 5% triggers corrective action and retesting but never a sales stop, which is the main gain for Northwind. S5 turns the 8-per-100,000 level into a reporting and investigation trigger with recall left to regulator discretion and no mandatory numeric recall, which benefits Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9. S3 gives a six-year retrofit window and S4 a 36-month suppression deadline, both within the acceptable ranges.
